'''Vladimir Radmanović''' ([[Serbian Cyrillic alphabet|Serbian Cyrillic]]: Владимир Радмановић; born 19 November 1980) is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player.

In Serbia he played for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP]] and in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) he was a member of the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Atlanta Hawks]] and [[Chicago Bulls]].

Radmanović also represented his [[Serbia and Montenegro men's national basketball team|national team]] most notably at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]].

'''Vitalii Mykolayovych Potapenko'''<ref name=nbabio/> ({{IPAc-en|p|oʊ|ˈ|t|ɑː|p|ɛ|ŋ|k|oʊ}} {{respell|poh|TAH|peng|koh}},<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide
 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> {{langx|uk|Віталій Миколайович Потапенко}}; born March 21, 1975) is a Ukrainian professional [[basketball]] coach and former  player who is an assistant coach for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State Raiders]] and was selected 12th overall by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[1996 NBA draft]], also the last pick before [[Kobe Bryant]]. Nicknamed "the Ukraine Train",<ref name=nbabio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vitaly_potapenko/bio.html|title=Vitaly Potapenko Bio|publisher=NBA|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080405161045/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vitaly_potapenko/bio.html|archivedate=April 5, 2008}}</ref> he played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], the [[Boston Celtics]], the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], and the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the NBA, as well as [[MMT Estudiantes]] in the Spanish [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=Spain&Team=198&Page=4 MMT Estudiantes former players]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.celticslife.com/2010/05/what-hell-happened-tovitaly-potapenko.html|title = What the Hell Happened to...Vitaly Potapenko?}}</ref>

Since retiring as a player, Potapenko has been serving as an assistant coach for several teams, among them the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]], the [[Indiana Pacers]], the [[Dakota Wizards]],<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/215728/Dakota_Wizards_Hire_Potapenko_As_Assistant_Coach Dakota Wizards Hire Potapenko As Assistant Coach]</ref> and the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] and later as an assistant director of player development for the Cleveland Cavaliers,<ref>{{cite web|title=Vitaly Potapenko returning to Cleveland Cavaliers as player-development coach|date=4 June 2013|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2013/06/ex-cav_vitaly_potapenko_return.html}}</ref> helping them win their first ever NBA championship.

'''Vincent Raymond Yarbrough''' (born March 21, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[NBA]] and Europe.

The 6'7" and 210 lb forward out of the [[University of Tennessee]] was selected as the fourth pick of the second round (33rd overall) of the [[2002 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2002.html |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played 59 games with them during [[2002-03 NBA season|2002–03]] (his only season in the NBA), averaging 6.9 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vincent Yarbrough 2002-03 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/yarbrvi01/gamelog/2003/ |access-date=2025-10-11 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Yarbrough's final NBA game was on April 16, 2003, in a 84–89 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]] where he recorded 8 points, 9 rebounds and 8 assists.

Yarbrough also played with [[Basketball Club Oostende|Oostende]] of the [[Belgium|Belgian]] basketball league and in [[Serie A (basketball)|Italy]] with [[Pallacanestro Messina|Sicilia Messina]] and [[Viola Reggio Calabria]].

In the 2006–07 season, Yarbrough played for the [[Germany|German]] team [[Brose Baskets]] in [[Bamberg]], [[Bavaria]] after signing for the team in July 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://217.13.116.51/imprimible/imprimir_noticia.jsp?temporada=E05&jornada=27&id=610 |title=Bamberg brings in Vincent Yarbrough |access-date=August 8, 2007 |archive-date=October 6, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071006094026/http://217.13.116.51/imprimible/imprimir_noticia.jsp?temporada=E05&jornada=27&id=610 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 2008, Yarbrough was signed by [[Telekom Baskets Bonn]] for the 2008–09 season.<ref>[http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/33862/448/bonn-brings-in-forward-vincent-yarbrough Bonn brings in forward Vincent Yarbrough]</ref>

'''Victor Wembanyama''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|w|ɛ|m|b|ə|n|ˈ|j|ɑː|m|ə}} {{respelling|WEM|bən|YAH|mə}};<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=24 October 2023 |access-date=17 May 2024}}</ref> {{IPA|fr|viktɔʁ wɛmbanjama|lang}}; born 4 January 2004), nicknamed "'''Wemby'''"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Randall |title=Victor Wembanyama Sets Course to Become a Basketball Billionaire Unlike Any Other |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2024-01-05/how-wemby-can-make-1-billion-in-basketball-earnings-in-nba-career |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |access-date=5 January 2024 |date=5 January 2024 |archive-date=5 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240105000546/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2024-01-05/how-wemby-can-make-1-billion-in-basketball-earnings-in-nba-career |url-status=live }}</ref> and "'''the Alien'''",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodson |first=Aaron |date=26 July 2024 |title=How Victor Wembanyama's unearthly size and still-growing feet made him Nike's 'Alien' |url=https://andscape.com/features/victor-wembanyama-nike-alien-logo/ |access-date=2 February 2025 |website=Andscape |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Erin |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama 'Not Really a Big Fan' of Unicorn Nickname; Prefers 'Alien' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10096656-spurs-victor-wembanyama-not-really-a-big-fan-of-unicorn-nickname-prefers-alien |access-date=2 February 2025 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the Spurs in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and is considered one of the best basketball prospects ever due to his rare combination of height, agility, and skills.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 June 2023 |last=Adi  |first=Joseph |title=Ranking the 20 best NBA Draft prospects since LeBron: Victor Wembanyama, AD, Zion at top with Scoot sliding in |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/ranking-the-20-best-nba-draft-prospects-since-lebron-victor-wembanyama-ad-zion-at-top-with-scoot-sliding-in/ |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> 

Wembanyama began his professional career at age 15 with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] in 2019. Two years later, he moved to [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the [[2022–23 Pro A season|2022–23 season]], Wembanyama signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] and became the youngest player to win the [[LNB Pro A MVP|Pro A MVP]] award, while earning [[LNB Pro A Best Defender|Pro A Best Defender]] honours and leading the league in scoring, [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and [[block (basketball)|blocks]]. He was unanimously named an [[LNB All-Star]] twice, winning the All-Star Game MVP once, and was a three-time [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player|Pro A Best Young Player]] from 2021 to 2023.

Following a historic rookie season in the NBA in which he led the league in [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game, Wembanyama was unanimously named the [[2023–24 NBA season|2024]] [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]] and became the first rookie and youngest player ever to be named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive First Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=Andrew |date=6 May 2024 |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama voted unanimous Rookie of Year |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40096225/spurs-victor-wembanyama-named-unanimous-rookie-year |access-date=7 May 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2024 |title=Rudy Gobert wins record-tying 4th Defensive Player of the Year award. Victor Wembanyama finishes 2nd |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-defensive-player-of-year-rudy-gobert-wembanyama-1d7846b4f8094579906c09619134bda1 |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], Wembanyama became the youngest and first unanimous winner of the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama named 2025-26 Kia NBA Defensive Player of the Year {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-2025-26 |access-date=20 April 2026 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Soto |first=Andrés |date=20 April 2026 |title=Victor Wembanyama makes history as NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/spurs/2026/04/20/san-antonio-spurs-victor-wembanyama-defensive-player-year/89694655007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422024818/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/spurs/2026/04/20/san-antonio-spurs-victor-wembanyama-defensive-player-year/89694655007/ |archive-date=22 April 2026 |access-date=30 April 2026 |work=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> That same year, he led the Spurs to the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in his first postseason appearance.

Wembanyama also plays for the [[France men's national basketball team|French national team]], with whom he won a silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. At the youth level, he led his team to two silver medals, including at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], where he set the [[FIBA]] record for blocks per game in a single tournament.
